title: Detecting RNA–Protein Interactions With EGFP-Cy3 FRET by Acceptor Photobleaching
protocol: Construct or obtain expression plasmids for RNA and protein interaction studies.
Ensure fusion proteins are in-frame with EGFP or other VFP.
Fusion at the C-terminus is preferred to ensure proper protein folding.
Select suitable FRET pairs for the designed experiments with higher quantum yield for the donor.
Choose fluorophores with better photostability and integral R0 values.
Consider using brighter alternatives to Cy3, such as Alexa Fluor 555 from ThermoFisher Scientific.
Label RNA using Alexa Fluor 555 instead of Cy3 due to its similar excitation and emission spectra but higher brightness and photostability.
Perform experiments to assess the functionality of the fusion protein and the mutant RNA.
Conduct intracellular co-localization by fluorescence microscopy.
Carry out RNA-IP for supportive biochemical evidence.
Rescue altered function after overexpression of the fusion protein in cells.
Construct or obtain plasmids as negative FRET controls.
Obtain unconjugated EGFP or an empty vector for control experiments.
Perform transfections using standard procedures or nucleofection with obtained plasmids.
Transfect cells to achieve five different coverslips containing Protein-EGFP and RNA foci, Protein-EGFP alone, RNA foci alone, unconjugated EGFP and RNA foci, and unconjugated EGFP alone.
Allow transfected cells to grow on no. 1.5 glass coverslips in a 6-well plate until full expression of plasmids is attained (24-48 hours).
Allow cells to grow in humidified cell culture incubator with 5% CO2.
Coat coverslips with collagen coating solution according to manufacturer's guidelines.
Incubate coated coverslips for 2 hours at room temperature.
Aspirate the collagen coating solution and air-dry overnight before use.
Place treated coverslips in a 6-well cell culture plate.
Fix transfected DM1 cells with 4% paraformaldehyde.
Permeabilize fixed DM1 cells in cold 2% acetone in PBS for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Wash the cells with PBS three times.
Incubate the cells with 30% formamide in 2× SSC buffer at 37°C for 10 min.
Hybridize with Cy3 labeled (CAG)10 probe at 0.1 ng/µl for 2 hr at 37°C in hybridization buffer.
Wash the cells in 30% formamide in 2× SSC at 45°C for 30 min.
Wash DM1 cells with PBS three times, 10 min each.
Mount coverslips on a glass slide with Vectashield without anti-fade.
Alternatively, use Fluoromount G as the mounting medium to form a semi-permanent seal.
Configure the confocal microscope for EGFP and Cy3 imaging.
Prepare the Leica TCS SP5 X confocal microscope with WLL or comparable laser system for excitation.
Adjust the laser power to ensure quick photobleaching without affecting fluorophores during image acquisition.
Use a weaker laser like WLL at 100% or a stronger laser like Argon at 25%-50% power.
Select a 63× oil immersion objective with numerical aperture 1.4 and 5× zoom for imaging.
Ensure correct filters and dichroic are in the optical path for EGFP and Cy3 imaging.
Adjust AOBS to 500-550 nm for EGFP and 565-700 nm for Cy3 on Leica TCS SP5 X.
Select PMT2 for EGFP and PMT3 for Cy3.
Set the PMT gain to 650-750V, using 650v to avoid signal saturation after photobleaching.
Select 12-bit image on the acquisition-scan control window.
Choose sequential scan by frame for fixed cells (line scan for live cells).
Use Leica AP wizard or a comparable workflow for acceptor photobleaching FRET.
Perform steps 15-20 on the slides with protein-EGFP and then Cy3 alone, and then again with the protein-EGFP slide.
Optimize imaging parameters (laser excitation, PMT gain, offset, and emission filters) for dual confocal imaging of EGFP and Cy3.
Ensure no bleed-through or crosstalk between the 2 channels during optimization.
Prevent photobleaching of fluorophores during normal image acquisition.
Select field of view of cells using the bright field or phase contrast function of the microscope.
Load the protein-EGFP (or EGFP) slide first on the microscope stage.
Use the microscope ocular to find representative cells using a mercury vapor arc (or LED) lamp and the corresponding filter cube to EGFP or Cy3.
Focus the cells to the center of the Field of View (FoV).
Switch to the confocal acquisition mode.
Select the pinhole for EGFP to 1 airy unit.
Do the same for the Cy3 channel.
Turn on the 488 nm laser to 5%-20% acousto optical tunable filter (AOTF) depending on the intensity of the protein-EGFP (or unconjugated EGFP).
Make sure there are no saturated signals using the “glow over under” feature on the Leica TCS SP5 X or another comparable confocal system.
Set the detector or PMT gain between 650-750v for EGFP.
Ensure the gray level intensity does not exceed ∼2000 for EGFP on a 12-bit image depth.
Set the PMT gain and 488 nm laser excitation to avoid saturated EGFP signals after photobleaching.
Increase the PMT gain by an additional 50v if the gray level intensity of EGFP is lower.
Increase the 488 nm laser excitation by 1%-2% if necessary for EGFP signal enhancement.
Check the average background signal using a dark control and untransfected cells.
Select and set the offset to reduce background noise, in this case set to zero.
Consider reducing background noise from ECM-coated coverslips by adjusting the offset.
Use phenol red-free or DMEM fluorobrite basal media for live-cell imaging to keep background low.
Load the Cy3 slide and repeat steps 15-19 using the 552 nm laser to 10%-12% AOTF.
Save the optimized imaging parameters after completing steps 15-20.
Do not change the saved imaging parameters for subsequent imaging.
Place the slide "c" with the RNA foci-Cy3 acceptor alone (A) specimen on the microscope stage.
Focus the cells to the center of the stage using the microscope ocular.
Select the region of interest (ROI) over the RNA foci.
Set up the bleaching cycle with the 552 nm laser at 100% AOTF.
Optimize the bleaching cycle or number of iterations required to photobleach the acceptor molecules to background levels without photobleaching the donor.
Proceed with FRET data collection using double-labeled DA and control slides.
Use specimens a, b, d, and e from step 4 for data collection.
Include dark control with untransfected cells to measure background noise.
Apply optimized settings as described in steps 15-19 and 22-25.
Image at least 30-40 cells for independent ROIs.
Draw a 2 × 2 pixel ROI over the RNA foci using Leica TCS SP5 X AB wizard or similar software.
Quantify pre- and post-bleach intensities of donor and acceptor for slides a, b, d, and e from step 4.
Calculate FRET efficiency (E%) in targeted bleached ROIs using the formula $E = ( {1 - D\ Pre\ bleach/D\ Post\ bleach} )*100$.
Calculate FRET efficiency (E%) in non-targeted, non-bleached control (Ctrl) ROIs.
Calculate Expt-E% and Ctrl-E% in all 4 slides a, b, d, and e to assess FRET occurrence between target mutant RNA foci and MBNL1 protein.
Prepare plasmids, cell lines, transfection, and slides for FRET.
Skip steps of fixation and RNA-FISH if using modified alternate protocol.
Proceed to imaging in basic cell culture media without phenol red or other suitable imaging media like DMEM fluorobrite.
Use phenol red-free media to keep background noise low during imaging.
Photobleach the acceptor with whole or half of the cell to destroy most of the acceptor fluorescence signal for FRET analysis.
Prevent recovery of acceptor molecules from vicinity into targeted ROIs to avoid confounding effects on donor fluorescence and evaluation of E%.
Avoid contribution of EGFP donor mobile fraction from vicinity during photobleaching in live cells to prevent false positivity of FRET signal.
Prepare plasmids and cell lines for FRET as described in the Basic Protocol (steps 1-5).
Transfect cells with prepared plasmids.
Label endogenous RNA for live-cell imaging.
Skip fixation steps when using the alternate protocol.
Skip RNA-FISH steps when using the alternate protocol.
Wash cells expressing protein-EGFP and labeled RNA with PBS (three washes, each lasting 10 minutes).
Mount culture dish containing washed cells in DMEM fluorobrite onto microscope stage with live-cell imaging chamber or heated stage inserts under humidified gas flow.
Proceed with steps 8-30 as described in the Basic Protocol.
